notes.title: Patch 2018.0905 Notes
notes.content:
I've just released the first update for PSF 2019, based on feedback from users.

Update 2018.0905 (Sept 5, 2018)
If your career has a problem from the initial version, you should either simulate the entire current season or start with a new career.  However, I don't expect you to have any problems.

Fixes:
- several fixes to Career play when coaching or simulating individual games
- now correctly update Career History all the time
- now automatically advance to offseason when simulating super bowl
- fix display of divisions to vary by conference
- fixed OT rules for regular season and playoffs

Enhancements:
- Can now switch image sets on existing career!
- Can now switch image sets on the fly!
- Analyze Game now displays Point Spread (desktop versions)
- Default End Zones now use all caps on team name and nickname
- several cosmetic changes

notes.title: Customizing PSF 2019
notes.content:
I've implemented Steam Cloud, which is very handy for keeping your customizations and saved games, etc across machines.  However, I haven't had time to implement Steam Workshop yet.

So, I wanted to briefly explain how you'll customize PSF 2019 within Windows and MacOS.

At a high level, it's simply a matter of sharing leagues (binary files) and image sets (folders).  Your game has three subfolders under it, and the game will tell you the path when you click on the "Customizing PSF" button.  The folders are:
[list]
    [*]leagues (every league there is available to your game, just paste new ones there)
    [*]import_export (more on that later)
    [*]images (here is where you'll create subfolders)
[/list]

So, the game will already have
[list]
    [*]leagues
            2019_leagues.lgs
    [*]import_export
            2019_leagues.csv
    [*]images
           default/  (don't change these, you'll lose your changes)
[/list]

and you might add, say a set of real nfl images and another set of real college images, and maybe a set of fantasy images (orcs, elves, etc).  Heck, maybe a sci-fi set, you get the idea.

Each of those would go in a folder under "images" so now your game folder looks like this:

psf2019
[list]
    [*]leagues
        [list]
        [*]2019_leagues.lgs
        [*]2019_real_nfl_names.lgs
        [*]lotro_players.lgs
        [/list]
    [*]import_export
        [list]
        [*]2019_leagues.csv 
        [/list]
    [*]images
        [list]
        [*]real_nfl/ 
        [*]1977_images/ 
        [*]lotro/ 
        [*]scifi/ 
        [/list]
[/list]

and at any time, you can launch the "mini editor" for a league and change the name of its images folder, and it immediately starts using those images!
